inspected_anchors.finding: Version 1.5.4, AGPL-3, R floor and imported dependencies; declaration does not establish a resolved runtime.
Authentic license is GNU Affero GPL version 3.
Section 13 addresses source offers for modified versions used over a network, and combination with GPLv3 work.
README GPLv3 badge differs from the authenticated AGPL-3 declaration and license text.
Ordered histories, policy/shifted precedence, finite-history k, cluster ID, sampling weights, cross-fitting and documented result semantics.
TMLE builds a task and passes density ratios and sequential fits to theta_dr; it does not itself return a treatment contrast.
Supplied shifted data overrides shift; censoring becomes one and each shift function reads the original data argument.
ipsi applies a randomized binary risk-ratio-style modification, with separate up/down branches; it is not the odds-tilt map.
Task checks finite weights, constructs/rescales outcome bounds, makes folds and normalizes weights; constant-range behavior needs qualification.
Observed uses censoring=1, risk-free uses competing event=0, and at-risk combines previous-time outcome/competing-event states.
Outer folds read ._lmtp_id while as_lmtp_data writes ..i..lmtp_id; supplied weights are mean-normalized unless already normalized.
History construction depends on k and declared ordering; this is a computational restriction requiring a scientific sufficiency argument.
Missing treatment/covariates among relevant uncensored at-risk observations are rejected.
Shifted data may differ only in declared treatment/censoring columns and shifted censoring must be one.
Without cluster IDs the helper splits rows; with IDs it groups rows, may lower V, and V=1 uses the same training and validation set.
Nuisance learner CV checks the number of supplied unique IDs and forwards IDs to SuperLearner; this is distinct from outer cross-fitting.
Prediction bound is controlled by the actual tol call; NULL returns unbounded predictions.
Documented .bound=1e-5 differs from the function default 1e5; the control field is returned without a range bound.
Inspected TMLE predictions pass hard-coded 1e-05; no control$.bound read occurs in this source.
Fluctuation wraps glm in sw and update calls bound with its own default.
SDR prediction calls pass NULL and feed the sequential influence expression into the earlier-time pseudo-outcome.
Per-fold futures request seeded evaluation; recombined ratios are then trimmed.
Density-ratio denominator uses a 0.999 cap; followed-rule and censoring/risk states multiply the returned ratios.
bound clips to [p,1-p], trim uses one quantile over the supplied object, and sw suppresses warnings.
Survival conversion reverses binary coding; weight normalization checks a mean of one.
Sequential expression sums cumulative ratio-weighted residuals with na.rm=TRUE; distinguish structural missingness from unexpected failures.
TMLE and SDR use distinct weighted means, rescale, and call ife::ife with weights and task$id; returned key is estimate, singular.

limitations: Source-level proposal reference only. No downloaded R code, upstream tests, native adapter or dependency was executed.
This selected pre-cutoff repository revision declares 1.5.4; CRAN artifact equality, latest-release coverage and installed environment are unverified.
AGPL-3 package terms are authenticated; transitive rights and a proposed distribution/network arrangement remain to be reviewed.
Source findings about cluster names and control defaults require native reproduction before claiming observed package failure.
The ife variance/contrast implementation, SuperLearner internals, future RNG behavior and full survival delegates are not qualified here.
A finite history, cross-fitting option or density-ratio truncation does not prove exchangeability, support, nuisance rates or calibrated uncertainty.
The monetary example is exact authored arithmetic under a stipulated law, not package output, empirical validation or bank benefit.
This decision does not close longitudinal software coverage or grant product/repository adoption.
